arxiv-2001-05492.title: Outlier Detection Ensemble with Embedded Feature Selection
arxiv-2001-05492.creator: Li Cheng, Yijie Wang, Xinwang Liu, Bin Li
arxiv-2001-05492.description: Abstract Feature selection places an important role in improving the performance of outlier detection, especially for noisy data. Existing methods usually perform feature selection and outlier scoring separately, which would select feature subsets that may not optimally serve for outlier detection, leading to unsatisfying performance.

arxiv-2207-04891.title: Minimoon still on the loose Journal: MAPS
arxiv-2207-04891.creator: Hadrien A. R. Devillepoix, Seamus Anderson, Martin C. Towner, Patrick M. Shober, Anthony J. T. Jull, Matthias Laubenstein, Eleanor K. Sansom, Philip A. Bland, Martin Cupák, Robert M. Howie, Benjamin A. D. Hartig, Garry N. Newsam
arxiv-2207-04891.description: Abstract On Aug 22, 2016, a bright fireball was observed by the Desert Fireball Network in South Australia. Its pre-atmosphere orbit suggests it was temporarily captured by the Earth-Moon system before impact. A search was conducted two years after the fall, and a meteorite was found after 6 days of searching.

arxiv-2303-11467.title: On Buffer Centering for Bittide Synchronization
arxiv-2303-11467.creator: Sanjay Lall \footnotesymbol 1, Călin Caşcaval \footnotesymbol 2, Martin Izzard \footnotesymbol 2, Tammo Spalink \footnotesymbol 2
arxiv-2303-11467.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Sanjay Lall \footnotesymbol 1, Călin Caşcaval \footnotesymbol 2, Martin Izzard \footnotesymbol 2, Tammo Spalink \footnotesymbol 2. We discuss distributed reframing control of bittide systems. In a bittide system, multiple processors synchronize by monitoring communication over the network. The processors remain in logical synchrony by controlling the timing of frame transmissions. The protocol for doing this relies upon an underlying dynamic control system, where each node makes only local observations and performs no direct coordination with other nodes.

arxiv-2303-14914.title: Would the Trees Dim the Lights? Adopting the Intentional Stance for More-Than-Human Participatory Design
arxiv-2303-14914.creator: Ned Cooper
arxiv-2303-14914.description: Abstract . The 2019/20 Black Summer bushfires in Australia demonstrated the brutal and disastrous consequences of changing the technological world without considering linkages with the biophysical, ecological or human worlds. An emerging more-than-human design philosophy encourages designers to consider such interrelations between humans and non-human entities.

arxiv-2402-06461.title: Sequential Flow Straightening for Generative Modeling
arxiv-2402-06461.creator: Jongmin Yoon, Juho Lee
arxiv-2402-06461.description: Abstract Straightening the probability flow of the continuous-time generative models, such as diffusion models or flow-based models, is the key to fast sampling through the numerical solvers, existing methods learn a linear path by directly generating the probability path the joint distribution between the noise and data distribution.

arxiv-2501-11034.title: Generative Retrieval for Book Search
arxiv-2501-11034.creator: Yubao Tang, Ruqing Zhang, Jiafeng Guo, Maarten de Rijke, Shihao Liu, Shuaiqiang Wang, Dawei Yin, Xueqi Cheng
arxiv-2501-11034.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yubao Tang, Ruqing Zhang, Jiafeng Guo, Maarten de Rijke, Shihao Liu, Shuaiqiang Wang, Dawei Yin, Xueqi Cheng. In book search, relevant book information should be returned in response to a query. Books contain complex, multi-faceted information such as metadata, outlines, and main text, where the outline provides hierarchical information between chapters and sections. Generative retrieval (GR) is a new retrieval paradigm that consolidates corpus information into a single model to generate identifiers of documents that are relevant to a given query.

arxiv-2502-16340.title: Skyrmion Crystal in a Microwave Field
arxiv-2502-16340.creator: Dmitry A. Garanin and Eugene M. Chudnovsky
arxiv-2502-16340.description: Abstract Temperature and field dependences of the frequencies of uniform modes of the skyrmion lattice in a 2D ferromagnetic film with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, as well as their damping, are computed within the model of classical spins. We show that the magnetization of the film exhibits Rabi-like oscillations when subjected to the microwave field at resonance with the low-frequency mode.

arxiv-2505-14976.title: SDLog: A Deep Learning Framework for Detecting Sensitive Information in Software Logs
arxiv-2505-14976.creator: Roozbeh Aghili, Xingfang Wu, Foutse Khomh, Heng Li
arxiv-2505-14976.description: Abstract . Software logs are messages recorded during the execution of a software system that provide crucial run-time information about events and activities. Although software logs have a critical role in software maintenance and operation tasks, publicly accessible log datasets remain limited, hindering advance in log analysis research and practices.

arxiv-2509-04780.title: Sustainability Risks under Lotka-Volterra Dynamics
arxiv-2509-04780.creator: Yiren Wang, Tianhao Zhi
arxiv-2509-04780.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yiren Wang, Tianhao Zhi. The record-breaking heat in recent years, along with other extreme weather conditions worldwide has not only warned us about the devastating effects of global warming but also revived our interest in studying sustainability risks on a broader scale. In this paper, we propose a generalised model of sustainability risks characterising the economic-environmental-social nexus (EVS) based on a classic Lotka-Volterra framework. Compared to the World3 model proposed by Meadows et al.

arxiv-2509-09361.title: Convergences and Divergences: Einstein, Poincaré, and Special Relativity
arxiv-2509-09361.creator: Galina Weinstein
arxiv-2509-09361.description: Abstract Jean-Marc Ginoux’s recent book, Poincaré, Einstein and the Discovery of Special Relativity: An End to the Controversy (2024), seeks to close the debate over the respective roles of Poincaré and Einstein. Yet what is presented as an “end” may instead invite a more careful analysis of how similar equations can conceal divergent conceptions.

pmc-10573767.creator: Xuemei Wang, Tifeng Shan, Shaojun Pang, Gábor Kocsy
pmc-10573767.description: Iodide is accumulated by the brown alga Saccharina japonica at a high concentration and has been proven to be an inorganic antioxidant that plays an important role in oxidative metabolism. Vanadium-dependent bromoperoxidases (vBPOs) and iodoperoxidases (vIPOs), which catalyze the oxidation of iodide, are essential for iodine accumulation and metabolism.

pmc-10644508.title: How can peer teaching influence the development of medical students? a descriptive, longitudinal interview study
pmc-10644508.creator: Marijke Avonts, Katrien Bombeke, Nele R Michels, Olivier M Vanderveken, Benedicte Y De Winter
pmc-10644508.description: BackgroundPeer-assisted learning (PAL) – where students take up a teaching role at an early stage of their training—is widely used in medical curricula. Many qualitative studies have investigated the perceptions and benefits of PAL, but no studies have longitudinally explored how peer teachers experienced their development. This could allow for a better understanding of PAL.

pmc-11396563.title: Clinical features and management approaches for Urinary Incontinence in Older Adults: Evidence from Three Hospitals in Qatar
pmc-11396563.creator: Asma Abbas, Brijesh Sathian, Mostafa Elawady, Shafi Hashmath Ulla Khan, Amir Ibrahim Abdalla, Ahmed Hayati Mohamed Ahmed Hasabelgawy, Ardalan Abdolgafor Ghafouri, Susan Mohieldeen Osman, Abdelrahman Hamad O Alzubier, Osama Elnour Abdelnour Idris, Hanadi Al Hamad
pmc-11396563.description: BackgroundUrinary incontinence (UI) is a common medical problem that seriously affects patients' physical, psychological, social, and financial well-being. To identify the most effective drug management techniques, this retrospective study aimed to describe the demographics, etiology, and medical traits of people with UI.

Visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA) is recommended by the World Health Organization as a triage test for cervical screening, however its accuracy as a triage test has been questioned.

pmc-12467433.description: Isoniazid (isonicotinic acid hydrazide, INH) is a key drug used to treat tuberculosis (TB), which continues to be the world’s most lethal infectious disease. Nevertheless, the efficacy of INH has diminished because of the emergence of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) strains that are resistant to INH. Our goal in this study was to modify INH to reduce this significant resistance chemically.

pmc-12830965.title: Synthesis of δ-bismuth oxide stable at room temperature for use in industrial applications
pmc-12830965.creator: J. Camilleri, P. Zaslansky, N. Ramanan
pmc-12830965.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The current research reports an inexpensive and effective method of synthesising δ bismuth oxide stable at room temperature by reacting monoclinic α-Bi2O3 and 5.25% sodium hypochlorite at 100 °C. The resultant product was washed, dried and characterized using optical imaging, microstructural analysis by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), thermographic assessment (TGA), X-ray diffraction (XRD), infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), X-ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) and synchrotron XRD.

pmc-13280954.description: RNA subcellular localization is a key determinant of RNA function and regulation, yet existing computational approaches rely primarily on sequence or simplified structural descriptors, limiting their scalability to long transcripts, their ability to model inter-label dependencies, and their applicability across RNA types.

pmc-13371687.title: Simultaneous embolisation of uterine arteries and ovarian veins as a management for chronic pelvic pain due to pelvic venous disorders and adenomyosis
pmc-13371687.creator: Filip Szkodziak, Sławomir Woźniak, Piotr Robert Szkodziak, Krzysztof Pyra, Tomaszg Paszkowski, Michał Sojka
pmc-13371687.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Chronic pelvic pain (CPP) of gynaecological origin encompasses a heterogeneous group of disorders, among which pelvic venous disorders (PeVD) and adenomyosis are recognised contributors. Concomitant PeVD and adenomyosis may potentiate symptom burden and complicate management strategies. A 45-year-old parous woman was referred with a protracted history of CPP manifesting as lower abdominal, lumbar and hip pain, exacerbated by prolonged orthostasis and coital activity. Menstrual symptoms comprised dysmenorrhoea and menorrhagia complicated by iron-deficiency anaemia.

pmc-13506412.title: Case Report: Synchronous cutaneous and pineal metastases from gastric adenocarcinoma—inter-lesion biomarker heterogeneity and multi-line targeted therapy
pmc-13506412.creator: Qing Shen, Wanqian Zhang, Ying Chen
pmc-13506412.description: Gastric adenocarcinoma simultaneously metastasizing to the skin and pineal gland represents an extraordinarily rare clinical manifestation. Pineal metastases account for less than 1% of all adult intracranial tumors and seldom originate from gastrointestinal primary lesions, and this atypical metastatic combination frequently results in delayed diagnosis and complicated clinical decision-making.
